description: Recruiter-facing portfolio and career-positioning flow covering identity, case-study product reasoning, AI-assisted workflow proof, CV/link/source hygiene, truthful research evidence and rendered QA.

stages.purpose: Establish target-role positioning, recruiter audience, public identity/CV/link inventory, case-study evidence boundaries, technical truth and research gaps before changing the narrative.

gates.require: primary target role, seniority boundary, recruiter/hiring-manager audience, core differentiator and 5-second/60-second/10-minute scan goals are explicit
homepage, flagship/supporting work, case routes, CV files/links, GitHub identity, live/source/Figma/contact links and public scratch/version clutter are inventoried from current source
case-study user/outcome/technical claims are classified as verified evidence, proxy/desk evidence, hypothesis, planned validation, blocked or unknown; framework/stack claims match source

when direct-user evidence is needed but unavailable, the research decision map, participant criteria, protocol and evidence-ledger structure exist while findings remain empty/planned rather than fabricated

stages.purpose: Turn recruiter questions and verified project evidence into a distinctive portfolio narrative, case-study hierarchy and inspectable AI-assisted workflow proof.

gates.require: role identity, hero proposition, flagship order, case-study evidence structure, AI-assisted workflow explanation, scan-depth hierarchy and preserve/change decisions are concrete before broad implementation
flagship cases expose problem/context, evidence class, product reasoning, decision/trade-off, system/design response, working proof and validation/outcome boundary where applicable
AI section separates human-owned judgment from AI-assisted work and links to inspectable workflow/config/QA evidence where public and safe instead of relying on a generic tools list

when Figma proof is requested, the file exposes intentional page/section structure, foundations/tokens, reusable components and variants, auto-layout/responsive behavior, critical product states, prototype flows and reviewer/developer annotations instead of acting as a flat screen dump

stages.purpose: Implement recruiter-facing narrative and evidence changes while repairing source-of-truth links, CV/identity hygiene and maintainable responsive code.

gates.require: recruiter-critical case, CV, live, source, Figma and contact links are real routes/files or intentionally removed; placeholder # links do not remain on public critical surfaces
primary role identity and canonical recruiter CV are consistent across homepage/source/public files; legacy duplicates or confusing naming are migrated, removed or explicitly explained
public source does not retain verified-unused versioned code, internal scratch notes or unsupported technical claims that contradict the portfolio narrative

stages.purpose: Independently verify the recruiter scan path, links/routes, technical claims, evidence boundaries, responsive rendering, accessibility and public-source hygiene before release.

gates.require: actual rendered homepage and representative case routes are inspected at desktop/mobile viewports for hierarchy, overflow, broken media, navigation and critical interaction states
flagship/supporting case routes, canonical CV and other recruiter-critical links resolve; raw source does not depend on a hidden runtime patch to mask placeholder critical links
framework, design-to-code, accessibility, AI workflow and QA claims are backed by source/test/runtime evidence or explicitly narrowed
independent concepts, missing user research, missing analytics/business outcomes and other evidence gaps remain clearly labeled; no polished artifact is presented as proof of unmeasured impact

when Figma proof is requested, representative flagship flows are reviewable without hidden context; naming, components/variants, variables/styles, auto layout, states, responsive frames, prototype links and handoff notes are coherent and no obvious detached or duplicate artifacts undermine the senior-craft claim

policies.reason: Recruiter-path QA found a material rendering, link, claim or source-hygiene defect; repair the owning implementation/source layer before re-verifying.
Positioning or case-study hierarchy remains generic/unclear; deepen recruiter narrative and design critique before implementation.
A career, project, research or technical assumption was invalidated; return to public/source evidence rather than patching the story downstream.
Missing target-role/project truth or user evidence blocks a responsible claim; reframe the unresolved decision and evidence plan.
Portfolio source or positioning changed; re-ground project truth before further narrative/code changes.
Tool failure requires diagnosis/evidence rather than blind retry.
